entries.question: With every piece of evidence hidden, coffee made, ALICE and TIRED answered, if you answer DOG to the laundry-room noise, does the officer open the laundry room (yes/no)?
entries.why: PowerPyx/GamerGuides give only recipes (hide nothing + DOG = suspicious; hide all + WASHING MACHINE = fooled); officer wiki page says HEARD NOTHING or a timeout sends him in; no source states the meter values. Benchmark (K15w10 rule: weights DOG 2, WIND 1, WASHING MACHINE 0, HEARD NOTHING 3, threshold 3) says no for DOG, yes for HEARD NOTHING.

originals: With nothing hidden, does WASHING MACHINE still get him to leave?
entries.question: With no evidence hidden (door opened in time, Luther and Alice upstairs), does WASHING MACHINE still make the officer leave (yes/no)?
entries.why: IGN: evidence can be left out 'without the police officer really caring too much'; PowerPyx's suspicious recipe uses DOG. Benchmark: no answer fools him once three or more evidence items are out.

entries.question: In one replay with the meter on screen: does skipping the coffee raise it, and does UPSET (instead of TIRED) raise it (yes/no for each)?
entries.why: Template prints Adam's stammer 'The… The androids, they…' unconditionally (so his line never changes), and gives no suspicion data. PowerPyx's suspicious recipe includes 'Don't make him coffee'; the Adam wiki page says nervousness raises suspicion unless dismissed as exhaustion. Benchmark: +1 for no coffee, +1 UPSET, +1 NOT MINE; TALK TO ADAM, REASSURE/THREATEN/CALM and YES/NO have no effect.

entries.topic: Hiding upstairs can still end in the laundry-room death
originals: Hiding upstairs and the death ending?
entries.answer: Yes. PowerPyx's last (blue) path runs UPSTAIRS > … > POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS > COP FINDS ANDROIDS IN THE LAUNDRY ROOM > LUTHER DIED SAVING OTHER DEVIANTS; its text also gets the same ending with Luther in the kitchen behind a drawn curtain. Only kitchen + open curtain (or no order) gives the kitchen death.
entries.source: flowchart mt-5.jpg (UPSTAIRS filled blue), mt-7.jpg (suspicious/laundry/ending filled blue); pp.txt 'I told Luther to hide in the kitchen and then closed the curtain to get this outcome'

originals: Hiding in the laundry room?
…Does hiding Luther and Alice in the laundry room?
entries.answer: The hiding place itself causes no discovery: IGN 'The only place that can get you into trouble is in the kitchen'. If the officer ends suspicious he opens the laundry room, and the chart has a single outcome for that branch (COP FINDS ANDROIDS IN THE LAUNDRY ROOM > LUTHER DIED SAVING OTHER DEVIANTS); there is no other ending tile.
entries.source: ign.txt 'Hiding Luthor and Alice: The only place that can get you into trouble is in the kitchen'; mt-7.jpg three ending tiles only

originals: POLICEMAN QUESTIONS ADAM?
entries.answer: It happens on the suspicious path too: the node is filled blue on PowerPyx's last run, which ended POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS; the template prints the questioning outside any condition group.
entries.source: flowchart mt-6.jpg (POLICEMAN QUESTIONS ADAM blue alongside POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS); template section open-door, 'What's your name, son?' unconditional

originals: The magazine's starting page?
Does the magazine lie open at the advertisement when Kara never reads it…
entries.answer: If Kara never reads it, the officer does not see the article: PowerPyx's last run has READ MAGAZINE grey and POLICEMAN SEES ARTICLE grey. CHANGE MAGAZINE COVER needs a prior read (PowerPyx: 'Works only if you read the magazine on kitchen table before').
entries.source: flowchart mt-4.jpg (READ MAGAZINE grey on the blue run), mt-6.jpg (POLICEMAN SEES ARTICLE grey); pp.txt Change Magazine Cover line

originals: ALICE vs NOBODY?
Upstairs after ALICE?
Does ALICE (rather than NOBODY) avoid the suspicion when they hide upstairs?
entries.answer: The chart draws POLICEMAN SUSPICIOUS ABOUT UPSTAIRS as a child of LIE ABOUT ALICE, so the suspicion node follows NOBODY (with Luther upstairs) only; after ALICE the template gives the harmless 'Hm, your daughter seems to have woken up.' NOBODY with another hiding place has no follow-up node.
entries.source: flowchart mt-6.jpg edge LIE ABOUT ALICE > POLICEMAN SUSPICIOUS ABOUT UPSTAIRS; template variants 'Luther is hidden upstairs and chose NOBODY / ALICE'

originals: The fooled arrows have the right size but the wrong trigger?
entries.answer: Template applies Alice SmallUp + Luther SmallUp in the 'Policeman is fooled' variant after the noise prompt. The rebuild applies h.alice(1); h.luther(1) in K15y (POLICEMAN FOOLED), not on a hide-all roll.
entries.source: template open-door, variant 'Policeman is fooled' ARROW Alice SmallUp / Luther SmallUp; ch25.mjs consequence K15y

originals: Do the two ending deaths both trigger Adam's hostility?
entries.answer: Yes. Luther kills the officer in both: the officer's wiki page says in the pantry he 'also dies as Luther will shove him', and in the laundry 'Luther will attack him, which also results in … the officer dying'; the template's suspicious variant has Adam 'He's dead! You killed him!'. Leaving Detroit's condition is 'Luther killed the cop in Midnight Train'. Benchmark sets midnightOfficerDead in both and ch32.mjs reads it.
entries.source: Police_Officer_0617 wiki page; ch32.1 template condition 'Luther killed the cop in Midnight Train'; ch25 template suspicious variant
